title: Medaka Kuroiwa is Impervious to My Charms
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Mona Kawai, used to every boy adoring her, sets out to win over transfer student Medaka Kuroiwa, who seems immune. Medaka is a monk-in-training at his family's temple, forbidden by his masters from falling in love, and resists her with prayer, mantras and cold water while Mona falls for him herself. Kodansha USA publishes it in English; age rating to verify.
life_message: It holds up sincere feeling over vanity, and playfully tests whether religious discipline can withstand love.

content.note: Underwear flashes, bodies pressed together, bunny-girl and nurse costumes used to tempt Medaka (Wikipedia; AniList Ecchi genre, MangaDex suggestive).
Deliberate seduction attempts on a boy who has asked to be left alone, played for comedy (Wikipedia).

dominant: Dharmic (temple vow) versus Hedonism (temptation), Expressive individualism

delivery.note: The clash between religious restraint and romance is played as a comedy contest rather than argued.

winners_losers: Mona wins Medaka's attention and her own sincerity, while the temple's rule against love is steadily worn down; rivals Asahi and Tomo add competition. Sympathy goes to romantic feeling over religious restraint.
